method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text with the writing-l4-rules skill (and references/regulative.md), from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18 and the rulings on negatives of 2026-11-04 and 2026-11-05 (JUST FALSE where the text says no, NOTHING with a NOTHING-kind tag where it does not answer); dates in a small module (built-in date functions, no daydate), the rules in one module and the complainant's questions in a seat module importing it; four regulative rules (s 93(2), s 96B(2), s 95B(1)(c), s 95A(3)) run by EVALTRACE inside exported questions that take only plain facts; no REFUSE; checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
edition_encoded: Equal Opportunity Act 1984 (SA), the South Australian register's current unauthorised RTF, version 1.4.2025, as deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/equal-opportunity-act-1984.txt (text sha256 0251b7e8100ae843e3857000c14a73ea6100a0f34e6e8d7d272567610bf5b4cd per the meta), retrieved from legislation.sa.gov.au on 2026-11-06 (the official register, not the Open Australian Legal Corpus); no regulations deposited or needed for a number

seat: the complainant: the person discriminated against, sexually harassed or victimised at work or in seeking work (job applicant, employee or unpaid worker, commission agent, independent contractor, contract worker, partner), who complains to the Commissioner for Equal Opportunity and takes it on to SAET or the Tribunal (saeo-seat.l4); the employer, principal and firm, the Commissioner, SAET, the Tribunal and the Supreme Court get no seat

checks.l4: stable l4 of VS Code extension legalese.l4-vscode 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset
checks.command: l4 run saeo-dates.l4 ; l4 run saeo-rules.l4 ; l4 run saeo-seat.l4 ; l4 run saeo-cases.l4
checks.result: 224 assertions written, 224 satisfied, 0 errors, 0 warnings in every file (2026-11-07)
checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics were read; satisfied assertions were counted by distinct source range; two deliberately wrong assertions were run once in a scratch file (since deleted) to confirm a failure shows as DiagnosticSeverity_Error. Expected values worked by hand from the text.

scope: Focus: the provisions a claimant meets (employment and discrimination). In: s 5(1) disability (and employee, employer in glosses), s 5(3)-(4); s 6(2)-(4); criteria ss 29, 51, 66, 85A, 85T; the work Divisions in full (Part 3 Div 2 ss 30-34, Part 4 Div 2 ss 52-56, Part 5 Div 2 ss 67-71, Part 5A Div 2 ss 85B-85F with s 85EA, Part 5B Div 2 ss 85U-85Z); the general exemptions so far as they reach work (ss 45, 47, 50, 64, 65, 79, 79A, 80, 82, 84, 85N, 85P, 85ZI-85ZO) and a s 92 exemption; s 86; s 87(1), (7), (9); ss 90, 91; s 93(1)-(2b), (4); s 95A; s 95B(1)-(3); s 96(1)-(3b); s 96B; s 98A(1)-(3)(b); s 100(2)-(5). Out: Part 1 machinery, Part 2, Part 6A, Part 7 procedure, ss 104, 106; Divisions 3-6 of each Part (associations, qualifying bodies, education, land, goods and services, accommodation, superannuation) and their exemptions; s 86A, s 87(2)-(6g), (8), ss 87A, 87B, 88 (its (a) civil rule reaches work but the work question covers assistance animals under s 66(e)), 88A, 89; ss 93AA, 93A, 94, 95, 95C, 95D, 96A, 96C, 97, 98, 98B, 98C, 99, 102, 103; appeals from SAET. Reasons in NOTES.md.
